subject: Follow-up: anomalous token counts on Nov 29 billing - proposed credit & remediation

Subject: Unexpected jump on Nov 29 invoice — possible double-counting

Monica,

We're seeing a large spike on our Nov 29 usage line — ~1.6M tokens billed in a 2-hour window, when our normal daily is ~120k. Attached is a brief ledger export. Can you confirm whether this is expected? If not, we'll need an immediate credit and explanation for our finance team.

I've copied our billing alias and Jared (ops) who is ready to provide more logs if helpful.

Thanks,
Nora James
Head of IT Ops
Nimbus Health

Nora — thank you for the ledger. I'm escalating immediately. Initial note: our incident tracker shows a short serving incident at 13:40 PST that affected request de-duplication for ~22 minutes. I'm opening a dedicated thread with our billing and engineering leads and will follow up within 2 hours with a proposed credit.

Immediate next steps:
- I'll pull the per-request logs and confirm whether the tokens were counted twice (monica).
- Marissa will draft a credit proposal we can send to Nimbus (marissa).
- Ben will validate whether any automated retries from the client side could have amplified counts (ben).

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the ledger attachment.

Best,

Subject: RE: Unexpected jump on Nov 29 invoice — proposed credit draft

Team — quick summary from engineering (pulled in via ops):
- Root cause: a de-duplication flag in the serving runtime failed to flip during a deploy at 13:39 PST, causing some inflight requests to be processed twice for 22 minutes.
- Impact: ~1.2M excess tokens attributed to Nimbus during window; some requests reattempted by client also present but not the primary cause.
- Mitigation: rollback at 14:01 PST; de-dup fix deployed and verified.

Draft credit proposal for Nimbus (suggested):
- Immediate one-time invoice credit for the excess tokens equivalent to $9,600 (calculated using their committed rate).
- A goodwill credits package: $2,500 account credit applied to December billing for disruption.
- Post-incident report and 30-day monitoring at no cost.

Attachments: redwood-credit-proposal.pdf (pdf, 24KB)

Please review numbers, Sean/Ben. If OK, Monica can send to Nora for sign-off.

- Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected jump on Nov 29 invoice — validation of client-side retries

Monica/Marissa — I sampled the request logs for Nimbus. Client-side retry rate is low; most duplicates are server-side repeat processing rather than client NC retries. Confirming Marissa's numbers are aligned with our log reconciliation. I recommend the $9,600 + $2,500 goodwill package.

I'll also request a billing flag to mark these tokens as 'incident-exempt' so they won't be considered for usage-based volume tiers in future calculations.

-Ben
Account Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Nora James <nora.james@nimhealth.com>, billing@nimhealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed credit & remediation steps for Nov 29 spike

Nora / Nimbus billing team — thank you for raising this. We investigated and confirm an internal serving regression caused a de-duplication lapse between 13:39–14:01 PST on Nov 29. Summary and proposal: 

What happened:
- A deploy introduced a timing edge in the de-duplication check causing duplicate processing for a subset of inflight requests.
- Root cause and timeline are attached in the post-incident snapshot.

What we propose (action required by you to accept):
1) One-time invoice credit of $9,600 to fully offset the estimated excess token charges for Nov 29 (will show on your Dec 1 invoice as a negative line item).
2) Goodwill credit of $2,500 applied to your account for Dec usage.
3) A post-incident report delivered by Dec 4 with detailed logs and mitigation steps.
4) A 30-day monitoring window where we will double-check token counts for your account and notify you of any anomalies.

Attachments: redwood-credit-proposal.pdf, nimbus-billing-ledger.csv

If this is acceptable, reply with a short confirmation and we will apply the credit and send the formal invoice adjustment. Apologies for the disruption — we value Nimbus as a strategic customer and want to make this right.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0186
